chunks: God will reward them for saying so with gardens where streams flow by, where they will live for ever. This is the recompense of those who do good.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific reward promised to those who do good in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific reward for the faithful who remained steadfast, with some scholars connecting it to the Ahl al-Bayt or the broader community of believers who accepted the Prophet's message despite trials. The phrase 'Jazā' al-Muḥsinīn' (reward of the doers of good) underscores the principle of divine justice (ʿAdl), where reward is not merely grace but a just recompense for consistent righteous action. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the integration of faith (Iman) and practice (Amal) in achieving eternal bliss.
